first: चौ॰ – नित नव सोच सती उरमारा। कब जइहउँ दुख-सागर पारा॥
en: Every day a new and heavy worry weighed on Sati's heart: 'When will I cross this ocean of sorrow? I insulted Raghupati and then took my husband's words to be false.'

first: सो फल मोहि बिधाता दीन्हा। जो कछु उचित रहा सेाइ कीन्हा॥
en: 'The Creator has given me the fruit of that, and he did what was right; but now, Creator, it is not right of you to keep me alive while Shankar is turned away from me.'

first: कहि न जोड़ कछु हृदय गलानी। मन महँ रामहिँ सुमिरि सयानी॥
en: The shame in her heart was beyond words; wise Sati remembered Rama in her mind and prayed: 'Lord, if you are called kind to the humble, and the Vedas sing that you remove distress,'

first: तो मैं बिनय करउँ कर जोरी। छूटइ बेगि देह यह मोरी॥
en: 'then I pray with joined hands, let this body of mine fall away soon, if my love for Shiva's feet is true in mind, deed and word, and this is my true vow.'

first: दो॰ – तौ सबदरसी सुनिय प्रभु, करउ सो बेगि उपाइ।
en: 'Then, Lord who sees all, hear me and quickly make a way for me to die without struggle, so that I am freed from this unbearable pain.'

first: चौ॰ – एहि बिधि दुखित प्रजेसकुमारी। अकथनीय दारुन दुख भारी॥
en: So the daughter of Daksha, lord of creatures, suffered a terrible grief beyond words; when eighty-seven thousand years had passed, the undying Shambhu came out of his meditation.

first: राम नाम सिव सुमिरन लागे। जानेउ सती जगतपति जागे॥
en: Shiva began to remember Rama's name, and Sati knew the Lord of the world had woken; she went and bowed at Shambhu's feet, and Shankar gave her a seat facing him.

first: लगे कहन हरिकथा रसाला। दच्छ प्रजेस भये तेहि काला॥
en: He began to tell sweet stories of Hari. At that time Daksha had become a lord of creatures; Brahma, thinking him fit in every way, had made Daksha the chief of all the lords of creatures.

first: बड़ अधिकार दच्छ जब पावा। अति अभिमान हृदय तब आवा॥
en: When Daksha gained such great power, great pride came into his heart; no one has been born in the world who does not grow proud on gaining power.

first: दो॰ – दच्छ लिये मुनि बोलि सब, करन लगे बड़ जाग।
en: Daksha called all the sages and began a great sacrifice; he invited with respect all the gods who receive a share of the sacrifice.

first: चौ॰ – किन्नर नाग सिद्ध गन्धर्वा। बधुन्ह समेत चले सुर सर्बा॥
en: Kinnaras, serpents, perfected ones, Gandharvas and all the gods set off with their wives; leaving out only Vishnu, Brahma and Mahesh, all the gods went in their fine sky-chariots.

first: सती बिलोके ब्योम बिमाना। जात चले सुन्दर विधि नाना॥
en: Sati saw many lovely chariots going through the sky; heavenly women in them sang so sweetly that sages hearing them lost their meditation.

first: पूछेउ तब सिव कहेउ बखानी। पिता जग्य सुनि कछु हरषानी॥
en: She asked, and Shiva explained it all; hearing of her father's sacrifice she was a little glad and thought, 'If Mahesh gives me leave, I could go and stay there a few days on this excuse.'

first: पति-परित्याग हृदय दुख भारी। कहइ न निज अपराध बिचारी॥
en: Her heart was heavy with the pain of her husband's rejection, but thinking of her own fault she said nothing of it; Sati spoke in lovely words mixed with fear, shyness and love:

first: दो॰ – पिता भवन उत्सव परम, जौँ प्रभु आयसु होइ।
en: 'Lord, home of kindness, there is a great festival at my father's house; if you allow, I would go with respect to see it.'

first: चौ॰ – कहेहु नीक मोरे मन भावा। यह अनुचित नहिँ नेवत पठावा॥
en: 'You speak well, and it pleases me,' said Shiva, 'but it is not right that no invitation was sent; Daksha has called all his daughters, but because of his quarrel with me he has left you out.'

first: ब्रह्म-सभा हम सन दुख माना। तेहि तेँ अजहुँ करहिं अपमाना॥
en: 'He took offence at me in Brahma's court, and so even now he insults me; Bhavani, if you go without being asked, there will be no regard, no love and no honour left.'

first: जदपि मित्र-प्रभु-पितु-गुरु गेहा। जाइय बिनु बोले न सँदेहा॥
en: 'It is true one may go without being asked to the house of a friend, master, father or teacher; but where someone holds ill will, going there does no good.'

first: भाँति अनेक सम्भु समुझावा। भावी बस न ज्ञान उर आवा॥
en: Shambhu explained in many ways, but by force of fate no understanding came to her heart; the Lord said, 'If you go without being called, in my view it will not go well.'

first: दो॰ – करि देखा हर जतन बहु, रहइ न दच्छकुमारि।
en: Hara tried hard and saw that Daksha's daughter would not stay; then the enemy of Tripura sent his chief attendants with her and let her go.

first: चौ॰ – पिता-भवन जब गई भवानी। दच्छ-त्रास काहु न सनमानी॥
en: When Bhavani reached her father's house, out of fear of Daksha no one welcomed her; only her mother met her kindly, and her sisters met her with many smiles.

first: दच्छ न कछु पूंछी कुसलाता। सतिहि बिलोकि जरे सब गाता॥
en: Daksha did not even ask how she was, and seeing Sati his whole body burned with anger; then Sati went and looked at the sacrifice, and nowhere did she see Shambhu's share.

first: तब चित्त चढ़ेउ जो सङ्कर कहेऊ। प्रभु-अपमान समुझि उर दहेऊ॥
en: Then she remembered what Shankar had said, and seeing her lord insulted her heart burned; the earlier pain had not filled her heart as much as this great anguish.

first: जद्यपि जग दारुन दुख नाना। सब तेँ कठिन जाति-अपमाना॥
en: Though there are many terrible sorrows in the world, the hardest of all is to be insulted by one's own family; seeing this, Sati grew very angry, and her mother tried in many ways to calm her.

first: दो॰ – सिव अपमान न जाइ सहि, हृदय न होइ प्रबोध।
en: She could not bear the insult to Shiva and her heart would not be calmed; then, firmly silencing the whole gathering, she spoke in anger:

first: चौ॰ – सुनहु सभासद सकल मुनिन्दा। कही सुनी जिन्ह सङ्कर निन्दा॥
en: 'Listen, all you members of this gathering and great sages: all who have spoken or listened to the slander of Shankar will reap the fruit at once, and my father too will deeply regret it.'

first: सन्त-सम्भु-श्रीपति अपबादा। सुनिय जहाँ तहँ असि मरजादा॥
en: 'The rule is that wherever one hears slander of the saints, of Shambhu or of Vishnu, one should pull out the slanderer's tongue if one can, or else close one's ears and run away.'

first: जगदातमा महेस पुरारी। जगत-जनक सब के हितकारी॥
en: 'Mahesh, enemy of Tripura, is the soul of the world, the father of the world and the friend of all; my dull-minded father speaks ill of him, and this body of mine was born of Daksha's seed.'

first: तजिहउँ तुरत देह तेहि हेतू। उर धरि चन्द्रमौलि बृषकेतू॥
en: 'So I will give up this body at once, holding in my heart the moon-crowned Lord whose banner bears the bull.' Saying this she burned her body in the fire of yoga, and cries of grief rose over the whole sacrifice.

first: दो॰ – सती मरन सुनि सम्भु गन, लगे करन मख खीस।
en: Hearing of Sati's death, Shambhu's attendants began to wreck the sacrifice; seeing it being destroyed, the great sage Bhrigu protected it.

first: चौ॰ – समाचार सब सङ्कर पाये। बीरभद्र करि कोप पठाये॥
en: Shankar heard all the news and in anger sent Virabhadra; he went and destroyed the sacrifice and gave all the gods the punishment they deserved.

first: भइ जग बिदित दच्छ-गति सोई। जसि कछु सम्भु-बिमुख कै होई॥
en: Daksha met the fate that is known in the world to come to anyone who turns against Shambhu; the whole world knows this tale, dear one, so I have told it in short.

first: सती मरत हरि सन बर माँगा। जनम जनम सिव-पद अनुरागा॥
en: As she died, Sati asked Hari for a boon, that in birth after birth she would love Shiva's feet; for this reason she was born again in the house of Himalaya, taking the body of Parvati.

first: जब तेँ उमा सैल-गृह-जाई। सकल सिद्धि सम्पति तहँ छाई॥
en: From the time Uma was born in the mountain's house, all powers and riches filled that place; sages made fine hermitages here and there, and the Himalaya gave them fitting places to live.

first: दो॰ – सदा सुमन फल सहित सब, द्रुम नव नाना जाति।
en: All the young trees of many kinds were always full of flowers and fruit, and many kinds of jewel mines appeared on the lovely mountain.

first: चौ॰ – सरिता सब पुनीत जल बहहीँ। खग मृग मधुप सुखी सब रहहीँ॥
en: All the rivers flowed with holy water, and birds, beasts and bees all lived happily; all creatures gave up their natural hatred and lived in love on the mountain.

first: सोह सैल गिरिजा गृह आये। जिमि जन रामप्रगति के पाये॥
en: With Girija in his house, the mountain shone like a man who has gained devotion to Rama; every day there was new joy in his house, and Brahma and the gods sang his fame.

first: नारद समाचार सब पाये। कौतुकहीं गिरि-गेह सिधाये॥
en: Hearing all the news, Narada came to the mountain's house out of curiosity; the king of mountains received him with great honour, washed his feet and gave him a fine seat.

first: नारि सहित मुनि-पद सिर नावा। चरन-सलिल सब भवन सिंचावा॥
en: With his wife he bowed his head at the sage's feet and had the whole house sprinkled with the water from his feet; he praised his own good fortune in many ways, called his daughter and placed her at the sage's feet.

first: दो॰ – त्रिकालभ्य सर्वग्य तुम्ह, गति सर्वत्र तुम्हारि।
en: 'Great sage, you know the past, present and future, you know all, and you can go anywhere; think in your heart and tell me the good and bad points of my daughter.'

first: चौ॰ – कह मुनि बिहँसि गूढ मृदु बानी। सुता तुम्हारि सकल-गुन-खानी॥
en: The sage smiled and said in gentle words full of hidden meaning, 'Your daughter is a mine of all virtues; she is lovely, simple, good-natured and wise, and her names are Uma, Ambika and Bhavani.'

first: सब लच्छन्न-सम्पन्न कुमारी। होइहि सन्तत पियहि पियारी॥
en: 'This girl has every good sign; she will always be dear to her husband, her married life will be firm forever, and through her, her father and mother will win fame.'

first: होइहि पूज्य सकल जग माहीं। एहि सेवत कछु दुर्लभ नाहीँ॥
en: 'She will be worshipped in the whole world, and nothing will be hard to get for those who serve her; remembering her name, women in the world will walk the sword's edge of faithfulness to their husbands.'

first: सैल सुलच्छनि सुता तुम्हारी। सुनहु जे अब अवगुन दुइ-चारी॥
en: 'King of mountains, your daughter has fine signs; now hear the two or four faults: her husband will be without qualities, without pride, without father or mother, detached and free of all doubt,'

first: दो॰ – जोगी जटिल अकाम-मन, नगन अमङ्गल-बेख।
en: 'a yogi with matted hair, free of desire, naked and in dress of ill omen; such a husband she will get, for such a line is on her hand.'

first: चौ॰ – सुनि मुनि-गिरा सत्य जिय जानी। दुख-दम्पतिहि उमा-हरखानी॥
en: Hearing the sage's words and taking them to be true, the couple was grieved but Uma was glad; even Narada did not know this secret, that the same words were understood in different ways.

first: सकल सखी गिरिजा गिरि मैना। पुलक सरीर भरे जल नैना॥
en: All her friends, Girija, the mountain and Maina thrilled in body and their eyes filled with tears; 'the words of the divine seer can never be false,' thought Uma, and she kept them in her heart.

first: उपजेउ सिव-पद-कमल सनेहू। मिलन कठिन भा मन सन्देहू॥
en: Love for Shiva's lotus feet rose in her, but a doubt came to her mind that meeting him would be hard; knowing the time was not right, she hid her love and went to sit again in a friend's lap.

first: झूठि न होइ देवरिषि बानी। सोचहिँ दम्पति सखी सयानी॥
en: 'The divine seer's words cannot be false,' thought the couple and the wise friends with worry; the mountain king took courage and said, 'Lord, tell us what can be done.'

first: दो॰ – कह मुनीस हिमवन्त सुनु, जो विधि लिखा लिलार।
en: The great sage said, 'Listen, Himavant: what the Creator has written on the forehead, no one, god, demon, man, serpent or sage, can wipe out.'

first: चौ॰ – तदपि एक मैं कहउँ उपाई। होइ करइ जौँ दैव सहाई॥
en: 'Still, I will tell you one way; it can work if heaven helps. Uma will surely get the kind of husband I have described to you.'

first: जे जे बर के दोष बखाने। ते सब सिव पहिँ मैं अनुमाने॥
en: 'All the faults of the husband I described, I see in Shiva; if she is married to Shankar, everyone will call even those faults virtues.'

first: जौँ अहि-सेज सयन हरि करहीं। बुध कछु तिन्ह कर दोष न धरहीँ॥
en: 'Hari sleeps on a bed of serpents, yet the wise find no fault in him; the sun and fire take in all kinds of things, yet no one calls them bad.'

first: सुभ अरु असुभ सलिल सब बहई। सुरसरि कोउ अपुनीत न कहई॥
en: 'All kinds of water, clean and unclean, flow in the Ganga, yet no one calls the Ganga impure; master, the mighty have no fault, like the sun, fire and the Ganga.'

first: दो॰ – जौँ ऐसहि इसिषा करहिँ, नर विवेक अभिमान।
en: 'If men, proud of their wisdom, try to copy such ways, they will fall into hell for a whole age; can a creature be equal to the Lord?'

first: चौ॰ – सुरसरि जल कृत बारुनि जाना। कबहुँ न सन्त करहिँ तेहि पाना॥
en: 'Knowing that wine is made with Ganga water, saints never drink it; yet when it flows into the Ganga it becomes pure; such is the difference between the Lord and a creature.'

first: सम्भु सहज समरथ भगवाना। एहि बिबाह सब विधि कल्याना॥
en: 'Shambhu is the naturally mighty Lord, and this marriage will bring good in every way; Mahesh is hard to win by worship, yet he is quickly pleased by those who endure hardship.'

first: जौँ तप करइ कुमारि तुम्हारी। भाविउ मेदि सकहिँ त्रिपुरारी॥
en: 'If your daughter does penance, the enemy of Tripura can wipe out even fate; though there are many grooms in the world, for her there is none other than Shiva.'

first: बर-दायक प्रनतारति-भञ्जन। कृपासिन्धु सेवक-मन-रञ्जन॥
en: 'He grants blessings, ends the pain of those who come to him, is an ocean of mercy and delights the hearts of his servants; without worshipping Shiva one cannot gain what one wants, even by millions of yoga practices and prayers.'

first: दो॰ – अस कहि नारद सुमिरि हरि, गिरिजहि दोन्हि असीस।
en: Saying this and remembering Hari, Narada blessed Girija and said, 'Now all will be well; give up your doubt, lord of mountains.'

first: दो॰ – अस कहि ब्रह्म-भवन मुनि गयऊ। आगिल चरित सुनहु जस भयऊ॥
en: Saying this, the sage went to Brahma's world; now hear what happened next. Finding her husband alone, Maina said, 'Lord, I did not understand the sage's words.'

first: जौँ घर बर कुल होइ अनूपा। करिय बिबाह सुता-अनुरूपा।
en: 'If the house, the groom and the family are fine, then marry our daughter to someone worthy of her; otherwise let the girl stay unmarried, my lord, for Uma is dear to me as my life.'

first: जौँ न मिलिहि बर गिरजहि जोगू। गिरि जड़ सहज कहिहि सब लागू॥
en: 'If we do not find a groom worthy of Girija, everyone will say mountains are dull by nature; keep this in mind, husband, and arrange a marriage that will not later burn our hearts.'

first: अस कहि परी चरन धरि सासा। बोले सहित सनेह गिरीसा॥
en: Saying this, she fell at his feet with her head down; the lord of mountains spoke with love: 'Fire may appear in the moon, but Narada's words will never prove false.'

first: दो॰ – प्रिया सोच परिहरहु सब, सुमिरहु श्रीभगवान।
en: 'Dear one, give up all worry and remember the Lord; he who made Parvati will bring about her good.'

first: चौ॰ – अब जौँ तुम्हहिँ सुता पर नेहू। तो अस जाइ सिखावन देहू॥
en: 'Now if you love your daughter, go and teach her this: let her do penance by which she may win Mahesh; by no other means will the trouble end.'

first: नारद बचन सगर्भ सहेतू। सुन्दर सब-गुन-निधि-बृषकेतू॥
en: 'Narada's words are full of meaning and have a reason; Shiva is lovely and a store of all virtues. Think of this and give up your doubt; Shankar is without stain in every way.'

first: सुनि पति-बचन हरषि मन माहीँ। गई तुरत उठि गिरिजा पाहीँ॥
en: Hearing her husband's words she was glad at heart and at once got up and went to Girija; seeing Uma, her eyes filled with tears and she lovingly took her on her lap.

first: बारहिँ बार लेति उर लाई। गदगद कंठ न कछु कहि जाई॥
en: Again and again she held her to her heart; her throat was choked and she could say nothing. Then Bhavani, mother of the world, who knows all, spoke in soft words that comforted her mother:

first: दो॰ – सुनहि मातु मैं दीख अस, सपन सुनावउँ ताहि।
en: 'Listen, mother, I had a dream and I will tell it to you: a handsome, fair and noble Brahmin gave me this teaching:'

first: चौ॰ – करहि जाइ तप सैलकुमारी। नारद कहा सो सत्य बिचारी॥
en: '"Daughter of the mountain, go and do penance, knowing that what Narada said is true; your mother and father also like this plan; penance gives joy and destroys pain and fault."'

first: तप-बल रचइ प्रपञ्च बिधाता। तप-बल विष्नु सकल-जग-त्राता॥
en: '"By the power of penance the Creator makes the world, by its power Vishnu protects the whole world, by its power Shambhu destroys, and by its power Shesha bears the weight of the earth."'

first: तप अधार सब सृष्टि भवानी। करहि जाइ तप अस जिय जानी॥
en: '"Bhavani, all creation rests on penance; know this in your heart and go and do penance."' Hearing this, the mother was amazed; she called the mountain and told him the dream.

first: मातु-पितहि बहु बिधि समुझाई। चली उमा तप-हित हरषाई॥
en: Having comforted her mother and father in many ways, Uma gladly set out for her penance; her dear family, father and mother were so upset that no words came from their mouths.

first: दो॰ – बेदसिरा-मुनि आइ तब, सबहिँ कहा समुझाइ।
en: Then the sage Vedashira came and explained everything to them all; hearing of Parvati's greatness, they were comforted.

first: चौ॰ – उर धरि उमा प्रान-पति-चरना। जाइ बिपिन लागी तप करना॥
en: Holding the feet of the lord of her life in her heart, Uma went to the forest and began her penance; her body was very tender and not fit for hardship, but remembering her lord's feet she gave up all comforts.

first: नित नव चरन उपज अनुरागा। बिसरी देह तपहि मन लागा॥
en: Every day her love for his feet grew new; she forgot her body and her mind was fixed on penance. For a thousand years she ate roots and fruits, and for a hundred years she lived on leafy greens.

first: कछु दिन भोजन बारि बतासा। किये कठिन कछु दिन उपवासा॥
en: For some days she lived on water and air, and for some days she kept hard fasts; for three thousand years she ate only dry bel leaves fallen on the ground.

first: पुनि परिहरे सुखाने सुखाने परना। उमहिँ नाम तय भयउ अपरना॥
en: Then she gave up even the dry leaves, and so Uma came to be called Aparna, 'without leaves'. Seeing Uma's body worn thin by penance, a deep voice of Brahma came from the sky:

first: दो॰ – भयउ मनोरथ सुफल तव, सुनु गिरिराज-कुमारि।
en: 'Daughter of the king of mountains, listen: your wish is fulfilled; give up this unbearable hardship, for now you will win the enemy of Tripura.'

first: चौ॰ – अस तप काहु न कीन्ह भवानी। भये अनेक धीर मुनि ज्ञानी॥
en: 'Bhavani, there have been many steady and wise sages, but none has done such penance. Now keep these fine words of Brahma in your heart, knowing them always true and pure.'

first: आवहिँ पिता बुलावन जबहीं। हठ परिहरि घर जायहु तबहीं॥
en: 'When your father comes to call you, give up your stubbornness and go home; when the seven great seers meet you, then know that these words are proved true.'

first: सुनत गिरा विधि गगन बखानी। पुलकगात गिरिजा हरषानी॥
en: Hearing Brahma's words spoken from the sky, Girija was glad and thrilled with joy. (Yajnavalkya said:) I have sung Uma's lovely story; now hear the lovely story of Shambhu.

first: जब तेँ सती जाइ तनु त्यागा। तब तेँ सिव-मन भयउ बिरागा॥
en: From the time Sati went and gave up her body, detachment filled Shiva's mind; he always repeated Raghunayak's name and listened to the tales of Rama's virtues wherever they were told.

first: दो॰ – चिदानन्द सुख-धाम सिब, बिगत मोह-मद-काम।
en: Shiva, who is awareness and bliss and the home of joy, free of delusion, pride and desire, roamed the earth holding in his heart Hari, the delight of all the worlds.

first: चौ॰ – कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिँ ज्ञाना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥
en: Sometimes he taught wisdom to the sages, sometimes he told the virtues of Rama; though free of desire, the wise Lord was grieved by the pain of parting from his devotee.

first: एहि विधि गयउ काल बहु बीती। नित नइ होइ राम-पद-प्रीती॥
en: In this way a long time passed, and his love for Rama's feet grew new each day; seeing Shankar's discipline and love, and the firm line of devotion in his heart,

first: प्रगटे राम कृतज्ञ कृपाला। रूप-सील-निधि तेज बिसाला॥
en: Rama appeared, grateful and kind, a store of beauty and goodness, with great radiance; he praised Shankar in many ways: 'Who but you could keep such a vow?'

first: बहु बिधि राम सिवहि ससुझावा। पारबती कर जनम सुनावा॥
en: Rama explained many things to Shiva and told him of Parvati's birth; the ocean of mercy described in full the very holy deeds of Girija.

first: दो॰ – अब बिनती मम सुनहु सिव, जौँ मो पर निज-नेहु।
en: 'Now, Shiva, hear my request, if you have love for me: go and marry the mountain's daughter; grant me this, as I ask it.'

first: चौ॰ – कह सिव जदपि उचित अस-नाहीँ। नाथ बचन पुनिमेटि न जाहीं॥
en: Shiva said, 'Though it is not fitting for you to ask like this, Lord, your words cannot be set aside; I must take your order on my head and obey it, Lord, for that is my highest duty.'

first: मातु-पिता-गुरु-प्रभु कै बानी। बिनहि बिचार करिय सुभ जानी॥
en: 'The words of mother, father, teacher and master should be obeyed without question, knowing them to be for our good; you are my greatest well-wisher in every way, and your order is on my head, Lord.'

first: प्रभु तोषेउ सुनि सङ्कर बचना। भगति-विवेक-धर्मजुत रचना॥
en: The Lord was pleased to hear Shankar's words, full of devotion, wisdom and duty, and said, 'Hara, your vow has been kept; now keep in your heart what I have said.'

first: अन्तरधान भये अस भाखी। सङ्कर सेाइ मूरति उर राखी॥
en: Saying this, he vanished, and Shankar kept that image in his heart; just then the seven seers came to Shiva, and the Lord spoke to them in very lovely words:

first: दो॰ – पारबती पहिँ जाइ तुम्ह, प्रेम परिच्छा लेहु।
en: 'Go to Parvati and test her love; then have the mountain king send for her to bring her home, and remove her doubt.'

first: चौ॰ – रिषिन्ह गौरि देखी तहँ कैसी। मूरतिवन्त तपस्या जैसी।
en: The seers saw Gauri there looking like penance in bodily form; the sages said, 'Listen, daughter of the mountain, why do you do such hard penance?'

first: केहि अवराधहु का तुम्ह चहहू। हम सन सत्य मरम सब कहहू।
en: 'Whom do you worship and what do you want? Tell us the whole true secret.' Hearing the seers' words, Bhavani replied in lovely words with a hidden meaning:

first: कहत मरम मन अति सकुचाई। हँसिहहु सुनि हमारि जड़ताई॥
en: 'My mind is very shy to tell the secret; you will laugh at my foolishness when you hear it. My mind is set and will not listen to advice; it wants to build a wall on water.'

first: नारद कहा सत्य सोइ जाना। बिनु पङ्खन्ह हम चहहिँ उड़ाना॥
en: 'Taking what Narada said as true, I want to fly without wings; see my foolishness, sages: I want only Shiva as my husband for ever.'

first: दो॰ – सुनत बचन बिहँसे रिषय, गिरि-सम्भव तव देह।
en: Hearing her words the seers laughed: 'After all, your body was born of a mountain! Tell us, who that listened to Narada's teaching ever kept a home?'

first: चौ॰ – दच्छ-सुतन्ह उपदेसेन्हि जाई। तिन्ह फिरि भवन न देखा आई॥
en: 'He went and taught Daksha's sons, and they never came back to see their home again; he ruined Chitraketu's house, and Hiranyakashipu met the same end.'

first: नारद सिख जे सुनहिँ नर नारी। अवसि होहिँ तजि भवन भिखारी॥
en: 'Men and women who listen to Narada's advice surely leave home and become beggars; his mind is false, only his body bears the marks of a saint, and he wants to make everyone like himself.'

first: तेहि के बचन मानि बिस्वासा। तुम्ह चाहहु पति सहज उदासा॥
en: 'Trusting his words, you want a husband who is detached by nature, without qualities, without shame, badly dressed, wearing skulls, without family or home, naked and wrapped in snakes.'

first: कहहु कवन सुख अस बर पाये। भल भूलिहु ठग के बौराये॥
en: 'Tell us, what joy is there in getting such a husband? You have been well fooled by a trickster. Shiva married Sati on the word of the elders, then left her alone and let her die.'

first: दो॰ – अब सुख सोवत सोच नहिँ, भीख माँगि भव खाहिँ।
en: 'Now Shiva has no worry; he eats what he begs and sleeps in peace. Can a wife ever stay in the house of one who by nature lives alone?'

first: चौ॰ – अजहूँ मानहु कहा हमारा। हम तुम्ह कहँ बर नीक बिचारा॥
en: 'Even now, listen to us; we have thought of a fine groom for you, very handsome, pure, pleasant and good-natured, whose fame and deeds the Vedas sing,'

first: दूषनरहित सकल-गुन-रासो। श्रीपति पुर-बैकुंठ-निवासी॥
en: 'without any fault, a store of all virtues, Lakshmi's lord who lives in Vaikuntha; we will bring such a groom to you.' Hearing this, Bhavani smiled and said,

first: सत्य कहेहु गिरि-भव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटइ बरु दोहा॥
en: 'You are right that this body was born of a mountain; my resolve will not break even if my body does. Gold too comes from stone, and even when burned it does not give up its nature.'

first: नारद बचन न मैं परिहरऊँ। बसउ भवन उजरउ नहिँ डरऊँ॥
en: 'I will not give up Narada's words, whether my home stands or falls; I am not afraid. One who has no faith in the words of a teacher cannot find joy or success even in a dream.'

first: दो॰ – महादेव अवगुन अवगुन भवन, बिष्नु सकल-गुन-धाम।
en: 'Mahadev may be a house of faults and Vishnu a home of all virtues, but whoever's mind delights in someone wants only that one.'

first: चौ॰ – जौँ तुम्ह मिलतेहु प्रथम मुनीसा। सुनतिउँ सिख तुम्हारि धरि सीसा॥
en: 'Great sages, if you had met me first, I would have listened to your advice and followed it; but now I have given my life to Shambhu; who will now weigh good points and bad?'

first: जौँ तुम्हरे हठ हृदय बिसेषी। रहि न जाइ बिनु किये बरेषी॥
en: 'If your hearts are so set on it that you cannot rest without arranging a match, there are many grooms and brides in the world, and matchmakers are never lazy.'

first: जनम कोटि लगि रगरि हमारी। बरउँ सम्मु न त रहउँ कुँआरी॥
en: 'My vow stands for millions of births: I will marry Shambhu or stay unmarried. I will not give up Narada's teaching, even if Mahesh himself tells me so a hundred times.'

first: मैं पाँ परउँ कहइ जगदम्बा। तुम्ह गृह गवनहु भयउ बिलम्बा॥
en: 'I fall at your feet,' said the mother of the world, 'please go home, it is getting late.' Seeing her love, the wise sages said, 'Victory, victory to you, Bhavani, mother of the world!'

first: दो॰ – तुम्ह माया भगवान सिव, सकल जगत पितु मातु।
en: 'You are maya and Shiva is the Lord; you are the mother and father of the whole world.' Bowing their heads at her feet, the sages left, thrilled with joy again and again.

first: चौ॰ – जाइ मुनिन्ह हिमवन्त पठाये। करि बिनती गिरिजहि गृह ल्याये॥
en: The sages went and sent Himavant, who pleaded with Girija and brought her home; then the seven seers went to Shiva and told him the whole story of Uma.

first: भये मगन सिव सुनत सनेहा। हरषि सप्तरिषि गवने गेहा॥
en: Hearing of her love, Shiva was lost in joy, and the seven seers went home glad; then wise Shambhu steadied his mind and began to meditate on Raghunayak.

first: तारक-असुर भयउ तेहि काला। भुज प्रताप बल तेज बिसाला॥
en: At that time there arose a demon named Taraka, with great strength of arm, might and power; he conquered all the worlds and their guardians, and the gods were left without joy or wealth.

first: अजर अमर सो जीति न जाई। हारे सुर करि बिबिध लराई॥
en: He could not grow old or die, so he could not be beaten; the gods fought him in many ways and lost. Then they went to Brahma and cried for help, and the Creator saw that all the gods were in distress.

first: दो॰ – सब सन कहा बुझाइ बिधि, दनुज निधन तब होइ।
en: Brahma explained to them all: 'The demon will die only when a son is born of Shambhu's seed; he alone will beat him in battle.'
